purpose: Trimipramine is used mainly to treat depression. It can help improve your mood, sleep, appetite, and energy levels. Sometimes doctors also prescribe it for anxiety or certain types of chronic pain.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate your mood. Trimipramine works by keeping more of these chemicals available in your brain so they can do their job better. It also has a calming, sedating effect, which can be especially helpful if depression is making it hard for you to sleep.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling very sleepy, dry mouth, blurry vision, constipation, dizziness especially when standing up quickly, weight gain, difficulty urinating, and feeling lightheaded. Many of these tend to improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal-like symptoms. Tell your doctor right away if you have thoughts of harming yourself, as antidepressants can sometimes increase these thoughts especially in young people early in treatment. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. It can cause serious problems if taken with certain other medications including MAO inhibitors. Let your doctor know if you have heart problems, seizures, glaucoma, or an enlarged prostate before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 75 mg per day, often taken as a single dose at bedtime because of its sedating effects. Your doctor may gradually increase the dose up to 150 to 200 mg per day depending on how you respond. Older adults usually start at a lower dose around 50 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
